article_content: New York (CNN) -- Four people died after a passenger vehicle entered a creek in the Queens borough of New York City, a Fire Department spokesperson said Saturday. The incident was reported late Friday night. Police officers discovered the car submerged in Steinway Creek, and Fire Department divers recovered four individuals. Darius Fletcher, 21; Jada Monique Butts, 19; Crystal Gravely, 19; and Jaleel Furtado, 20, all residents of East Elmhurst, New York, were pronounced dead upon arrival at local hospitals, according to the New York Police Department's news release. The driver, a 20-year-old male, is listed in stable condition at Elmhurst General Hospital, stated New York Police Department spokeswoman Annette Markowski. Investigators determined that the 2009 Honda Accord struck a curb on 19th Avenue before rolling into the creek, which is part of the East River. Fire Department spokesman Mike Parrella indicated that there was a drop of at least 5 or 6 feet from the street level to the water surface. The water level in the creek 'was sufficient to submerge the vehicle,' Parrella added.

Incident je prijavljen kasno u petak navečer. Policajci su pronašli automobil potopljen u potoku Steinway, a ronioci vatrogasne službe su izvukli četiri osobe. Darius Fletcher (21), Jada Monique Butts (19), Crystal Gravely (19) i Jaleel Furtado (20), svi iz East Elmhursta, New York, proglašeni su mrtvima po dolasku u lokalne bolnice, navodi se u saopćenju njujorške policije. Vozač, 20-godišnji muškarac, je u stabilnom stanju u Općoj bolnici Elmhurst, izjavila je glasnogovornica njujorške policije Annette Markowski. Istražitelji su utvrdili da je Honda Accord iz 2009. udarila u ivičnjak na 19. aveniji prije nego što se prevrnula u potok, koji je dio East Rivera. article_content: Togo international Emmanuel Adebayor scored a hat-trick as Manchester City secured their place in the knockout stage of the Europa League with a 3-1 victory over Lech Poznan at the City of Manchester Stadium. These were Adebayor's first goals of the season, reminding manager Roberto Mancini of his capabilities amid speculation linking City with a move for Manchester United's star striker, Wayne Rooney, in the upcoming January transfer window. If Rooney were to join City, he would reunite with Carlos Tevez. Tevez was rested by Mancini for Thursday's match against the determined Polish side. Adebayor gave City an early two-goal lead, but Lech responded with a goal from Joel Tshibamba shortly after halftime. Lech had opportunities to equalize before Adebayor completed his hat-trick late in the second half, assisted by David Silva. Adam Johnson nearly added a fourth goal with a solo effort, but the night belonged to Adebayor, who could have scored more. The win puts City top of Group A, ahead of Lech, with Juventus in third place following their 1-1 draw in Salzburg. In other action, Liverpool battled to a goalless draw against Napoli in Italy. A large police presence was evident at the San Paolo stadium following attacks on Liverpool fans before the game. Liverpool manager Roy Hodgson, under pressure due to their poor start to the Premier League season, fielded a young team without Steven Gerrard and Fernando Torres, who performed admirably. With five points from three games, Liverpool leads Group K and is favored to advance. 'We're experiencing a difficult period in the league, and things haven't gone our way for various reasons. That's why we're at the bottom and eager to improve,' Hodgson told AFP. Elsewhere in the Europa League, Porto earned their third win in three matches, triumphing 3-1 against Besiktas in Turkey, despite two players being sent off. Falcao opened the scoring, and Hulk added two more goals before Bobo scored a consolation goal for Besiktas. Paris St Germain remains undefeated in Group J after Clement Chantome scored a late equalizer against Borussia Dortmund, the Bundesliga leaders. Dortmund had taken the lead through a Nuri Sahin penalty. Sevilla is second in Group J, one point behind PSG, after a 1-0 victory at Karpaty Lviv, with Frederic Kanoute scoring the decisive goal.

article_content: Don't be too impressed by the smart skin being developed for robots; your own skin is surprisingly more capable. Recent findings indicate that neurons within human skin execute complex calculations, a function previously believed to be exclusive to the brain. According to researchers, our skin sends a significantly larger amount of information to the brain than was initially recognized. Skin is far more perceptive than we realized, relaying a wealth of information. Our sense of touch is processed initially by neurons in the skin before the signals are transmitted to the brain for further analysis. The study revealed that the skin independently computes geometric information before signaling the brain. Earlier understandings suggested that only simpler data was conveyed. A study published in 'Nature Neuroscience' by Umeå University in Sweden indicates that skin calculates geometric data before sending signals to the brain. Researchers from the Department of Integrative Medical Biology (IMB) at Umeå University discovered that this neuronal branching enables first-order tactile neurons to signal both the contact and geometric properties of an object. Andrew Pruszynski, a researcher involved in the study, stated that the first-order tactile neurons in our fingertips provide information about when and how intensely we touch an object, and also about its shape. The research demonstrates that a neuron's sensitivity to shape depends on the configuration of its highly sensitive areas. Pruszynski noted the most surprising result was that these peripheral neurons perform calculations akin to those done by neurons in the cerebral cortex when examining an object with a fingertip. Essentially, our touch experiences undergo preliminary processing in the skin before reaching the brain.
translated_content: Ne budite previše impresionirani pametnom kožom koja se razvija za robote; vaša vlastita koža je iznenađujuće sposobnija. Nedavna otkrića ukazuju na to da neuroni unutar ljudske kože izvršavaju složene proračune, funkciju za koju se ranije vjerovalo da je ekskluzivna za mozak. Prema istraživačima, naša koža šalje znatno veću količinu informacija u mozak nego što se prvobitno pretpostavljalo. Koža je daleko perceptivnija nego što smo shvatili, prenoseći bogatstvo informacija. Naš osjećaj dodira se inicijalno obrađuje od strane neurona u koži prije nego što se signali prenesu u mozak na daljnju analizu. Studija je otkrila da koža nezavisno izračunava geometrijske informacije prije signaliziranja mozgu. Ranija shvatanja su sugerisala da se prenose samo jednostavniji podaci. Studija objavljena u časopisu 'Nature Neuroscience' od strane Univerziteta Umeå u Švedskoj ukazuje na to da koža izračunava geometrijske podatke prije slanja signala u mozak. Istraživači sa Odjela za integrativnu medicinsku biologiju (IMB) na Univerzitetu Umeå otkrili su da ovo neuronsko grananje omogućava taktilnim neuronima prvog reda da signaliziraju i kontakt i geometrijska svojstva objekta. Andrew Pruszynski, istraživač uključen u studiju, izjavio je da taktilni neuroni prvog reda u našim vrhovima prstiju pružaju informacije o tome kada i koliko intenzivno dodirujemo objekt, kao i o njegovom obliku. Istraživanje pokazuje da osjetljivost neurona na oblik ovisi o konfiguraciji njegovih visoko osjetljivih područja. Pruszynski je primijetio da je najiznenađujući rezultat bio da ovi periferni neuroni obavljaju proračune slične onima koje obavljaju neuroni u moždanoj kori prilikom pregleda objekta vrhom prsta. U suštini, naša iskustva dodira prolaze preliminarnu obradu u koži prije nego što stignu do mozga.

article_content: By Martin Robinson PUBLISHED: 08:38 EST, January 10, 2014 UPDATED: 12:22 EST, January 10, 2014 A gym-loving benefit cheat who stole £21,000 after claiming she was too disabled to dress herself has been prosecuted after being filmed working out. Anne Bird, 60, was seen running, jumping, and bending by investigators who were tipped off that she had been going to circuit training, spinning classes, and Pilates for six years. Bird was handed a 12-week suspended jail sentence at Walsall Magistrates Court. Investigators set up a surveillance operation to monitor her exercise regime before prosecuting her, and found that she enjoyed strenuous exercise. Keeping active: Benefit cheat Anne Bird, 60, is seen here rolling on a Swiss ball, despite telling the DWP that she was too disabled to dress herself or get out of a bath. Bird, who suffers from a degenerative condition and has admitted to her fraud, had previously been a Royal Mail delivery worker but left in 2008 due to health problems. Nimble: The 60-year-old was seen exercising with a skipping rope at this leisure center session, stretching her back, arms, and legs. Maggie Meakin, prosecuting, told Walsall Magistrates Court that the defendant was overpaid a total of £21,109 after making false declarations on claim forms to obtain disability allowance. 'It was confirmed by a doctor that she has osteoarthritis and needs help to bathe and dress, and needed help to walk,' she said. 'She then applied for the higher rate of disability living allowance, claiming at this point that she needed help as she had problems with her knees and hips. The department was made aware that from October 2006 to August 2012, she was attending Bloxwich Leisure Centre and participating in group exercises, including Pilates and circuit training. She then upgraded her membership to sessions which included aerobics. 'In witness statements, the staff said they were aware she had problems with her knee, but she took part in spinning bike classes.' Bird, of Pleck, suffers from osteoarthritis in her legs and rheumatoid arthritis in her hands. She was entitled to some benefits, but not the full amount that was paid to her. She had previously denied two counts of dishonestly making a false statement to obtain a benefit but changed to guilty pleas earlier this week ahead of the matter going to trial. In sentencing her on Wednesday, magistrates jailed her for 12 weeks, suspended for 12 months, and handed her a six-month supervision order with probation. Shame: The cheat was also filmed doing rigorous sit-ups and press-ups while balancing on a fitness ball. Spared prison: Bird was handed a suspended sentence. She was also ordered to pay £300 in costs and an £80 victims' surcharge. Lee Preston, defending, said she had already repaid the money. 'She borrowed and also used her pension lump sum to repay the money. Her condition is degenerative. She will get less and less mobile as time goes on. 'The sums have long been repaid. She was following advice from her doctor and physiotherapist to exercise as much as possible. 'It is unlikely that she will ever appear before the courts again.' Zaynab Tarajia, representing the probation service, said Bird was unsuitable for carrying out unpaid work in the community due to her continuing health issues. She told the court Bird had explained that she had followed her GP's advice to exercise. She said: 'She admits that on occasion she exercised more than she needed to and admits that she should have told the DWP about her improved health, as she would have been entitled to benefits, but less than she received. She is extremely remorseful of her actions.' Bird is in receipt of carers' allowance regarding her husband's care and is now set to get advice over the correct benefits that she should be claiming for her own illness.

Prilikom izricanja presude u srijedu, sudije su je osudile na 12 sedmica zatvora, uslovno na 12 mjeseci, i izrekle joj šestomjesečni nadzorni nalog uz uvjetnu kaznu. Također joj je naloženo da plati 300 funti troškova i 80 funti doprinosa za žrtve. Lee Preston, branitelj, je rekao da je ona već vratila novac. ’Pozajmila je i iskoristila svoju penzionersku paušal kako bi vratila novac. Njeno stanje je degenerativno. Izuzetno se kaje zbog svojih postupaka.' Bird prima naknadu za njegu supruga i sada će dobiti savjete o ispravnim beneficijama, koje bi trebala tražiti za vlastitu bolest.

article_content: In South Florida, Arnold Abbott, a 90-year-old, encountered police while giving out four meals to individuals experiencing homelessness in a park. He was prevented from serving any further food. Abbott recounted that an officer demanded he drop the plate immediately, as if he were holding a weapon. Abbott and two pastors in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, were charged on Sunday for providing food to the homeless in a public space. These charges mark the city's first enforcement of a recently enacted ordinance that prohibits sharing food in public, according to WPLG, a CNN affiliate. WPLG reports that they could face imprisonment and a $500 penalty. Despite some criticism from advocates for the homeless, city officials have asserted that they will enforce the new regulations. Mayor Jack Seiler told WPLG, 'The fact that the media is paying attention will not stop us from enforcing the law. We enforce the laws here in Fort Lauderdale.' In an interview with the Sun-Sentinel newspaper, he defended the law. 'I am not happy with the cycle of homelessness in Fort Lauderdale,' Seiler stated. Seiler commented that 'Giving them a meal and keeping them in that cycle on the street isn't a productive approach'. Abbott, who has been assisting the homeless in the area since 1991 through his nonprofit, Love Thy Neighbor, stated that the authorities are singling out the city's most vulnerable people. He said, 'These are the poorest of the poor. They have nothing. They lack shelter.' Then he asks, 'Who can deny them help?' The city has also recently passed an ordinance restricting the storage of personal belongings in public areas, according to WPLG. Following that came the limitations on sharing food. Abbott stated, 'The city passed an ordinance requiring us to have a Porta-Potty. It's absurd. The entire thing was designed to rid Fort Lauderdale of its homeless.' Abbott reported that 'Police said to me that anyone who touches a pan, anyone who is involved, will be arrested.' Abbott has faced this battle before. In 1999, he sued the city for preventing him from feeding the homeless on the beach. He won the case, according to WPLG. He stated that the threat of being charged will not deter him from doing it again. He declared, 'I'm not afraid of jail. I don't want to go, but I will if I have to.' Abbott announced that on Wednesday, he would be at Fort Lauderdale Beach, ready to serve another meal.

article_content: As New York Yankee Alex Rodriguez faces a season ban for 2014, 60 Minutes examined the doping charges against him. In a show broadcast on CBS on Sunday, Anthony Bosch, the chief witness against A-Rod in the MLB case, claimed he injected the player with banned substances. A-Rod declined to participate in the CBS show; however, Anthony Bosch featured alongside Major League Baseball's Rob Manfred. Biogenesis founder Anthony Bosch alleged on 60 Minutes that he injected A-Rod with performance-enhancing drugs. The doping charges against A-Rod initially led to a 211-game suspension, which was later reduced on Saturday. The baseball player has denied using banned substances during his time with the Yankees and never tested positive for drugs while on the team. In 60 Minutes, Bosch alleges that he injected A-Rod with testosterone, insulin-like growth factor 1, and human growth hormone at least a dozen times. 'Alex was scared of needles, so at times, he would ask me to inject him,' Bosch claimed, adding that the player paid him $12,000 a month. Bosch also alleged that A-Rod inquired about the substances given to his former client, Manny Ramirez, as the New York Yankee aimed to achieve his dream of 800 home runs. Text messages between A-Rod and Bosch, reviewed by 60 Minutes, indicated daily contact at times. Bosch further claimed that A-Rod's associates attempted to intimidate him to prevent him from cooperating with the MLB investigation. Manfred stated on the show that the alleged threats appeared credible, 'particularly given that he identified individuals that we had our own concerns about'. Bosch initially denied providing players with performance-enhancing drugs but later cooperated with the investigation. The MLB dropped its lawsuit against Bosch and is covering his security and legal fees. A-Rod's lawsuit against the MLB describes this arrangement as a $5 million bribe, a charge that Manfred has denied. The 38-year-old player issued a statement on Saturday, asserting: 'I have been clear that I did not use performance-enhancing substances as alleged, or violate any agreements, and I will take this fight to federal court to prove it.'

article_content: Opposition officials say Russia and Syria are capitalising on the world’s focus on Gaza to escalate attacks in Idlib. Russian airstrikes have targeted Syrian rebels, and the United States has bombed Iran-backed groups in Syria. The Russian military has criticised Washington for failing to coordinate its operations. Reports indicate that Russian airstrikes in Syria’s Idlib province have killed 34 rebel fighters and injured 60, though these figures may vary. Russia’s Aerospace Forces claim to have hit “illegal armed groups” in Idlib responsible for an artillery attack on Syrian government positions, according to Rear Admiral Vadim Kulit, as reported by state news agency Interfax on Sunday. The positions of Syrian government troops were reportedly struck seven times in the previous 24 hours, the Russian official said. The Syrian army has blamed rebels for attacks on government-held areas in Idlib and Aleppo provinces. Syria denies indiscriminate shelling of civilian areas under rebel control. However, opposition officials say both Moscow and Damascus are taking advantage of the world’s focus on the war in Gaza to escalate attacks in the densely populated region. After 12 years of civil war, Idlib is Syria’s last rebel-held territory, with an estimated three million inhabitants largely refusing to live under the authoritarian rule of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad. Since the civil war broke out in Syria in 2011, reports indicate that more than half a million people have been killed, though estimates vary. Kulit also repeated frequent Russian claims that the US-led coalition had breached Syrian airspace, saying numerous jet and drone flights were not coordinated with the Russian side. The United States carried out two airstrikes against Iran-aligned groups in Syria, US Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin confirmed on Monday. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported that at least eight pro-Iran fighters were killed. Austin said that more strikes against Iran-linked groups could follow if attacks against US forces in Iraq and Syria continue. “These attacks must stop, and if they don’t stop, then we won’t hesitate to do what’s necessary, again, to protect the troops,” Austin told reporters at a news conference in Seoul. The US strike is the third in just over two weeks as Washington attempts to put an end to drone and rocket attacks against its forces in Syria and Iraq that began when the Israel-Hamas war started a month ago. US and coalition troops have reportedly been attacked at least 40 times in Iraq and Syria by Iran-backed forces in recent weeks. Approximately 56 troops have been injured in the attacks in Syria and Iraq, but the Pentagon reports that all have returned to duty. Follow Al Jazeera English:
translated_content: Opozicioni zvaničnici kažu da Rusija i Sirija koriste fokus svijeta na Gazi kako bi eskalirali napade u Idlibu. Ruski zračni udari su bili usmjereni na sirijske pobunjenike, a Sjedinjene Američke Države su bombardovale grupe koje podržava Iran u Siriji. Ruska vojska je kritikovala Washington zbog propusta da koordinira svoje operacije. Izvještaji govore da su ruski zračni udari u sirijskoj provinciji Idlib ubili 34 pobunjenička borca i ranili 60, iako se ove brojke mogu razlikovati. Ruske zračno-kosmičke snage tvrde da su pogodile 'ilegalne oružane grupe' u Idlibu koje su odgovorne za artiljerijski napad na položaje sirijske vlade, prema riječima kontraadmirala Vadima Kulita, kako je izvijestila državna novinska agencija Interfax u nedjelju. Navodno je položaje trupa sirijske vlade pogodilo sedam puta u prethodna 24 sata, rekao je ruski zvaničnik. Sirijska vojska je okrivila pobunjenike za napade na područja pod kontrolom vlade u provincijama Idlib i Alepo. Sirija negira neselektivno granatiranje civilnih područja pod kontrolom pobunjenika. Međutim, opozicioni zvaničnici kažu da Moskva i Damask iskorištavaju fokus svijeta na rat u Gazi kako bi eskalirali napade u gusto naseljenoj regiji. Nakon 12 godina građanskog rata, Idlib je posljednja teritorija u Siriji pod kontrolom pobunjenika, sa procijenjenih tri miliona stanovnika koji uglavnom odbijaju živjeti pod autoritarnom vlašću sirijskog predsjednika Bashara al-Assada. Od izbijanja građanskog rata u Siriji 2011. godine, izvještaji pokazuju da je više od pola miliona ljudi ubijeno, iako se procjene razlikuju. Kulit je također ponovio česte ruske tvrdnje da je koalicija predvođena SAD-om narušila sirijski zračni prostor, rekavši da brojni letovi aviona i dronova nisu koordinirani sa ruskom stranom. Sjedinjene Američke Države su izvele dva zračna udara na grupe koje podržava Iran u Siriji, potvrdio je američki sekretar odbrane Lloyd Austin u ponedjeljak. Sirijski opservatorij za ljudska prava izvijestio je da je najmanje osam boraca koji podržavaju Iran ubijeno. Austin je rekao da bi moglo uslijediti više udara na grupe povezane s Iranom ako se nastave napadi na američke snage u Iraku i Siriji. “Ovi napadi moraju prestati, a ako ne prestanu, onda nećemo oklijevati da ponovo učinimo ono što je potrebno da zaštitimo trupe”, rekao je Austin novinarima na konferenciji za novinare u Seulu. article_content: A judge in Wyoming sentenced a 75-year-old Missouri woman to life in prison on Monday for murdering her husband with a rifle in the mid-1970s and disposing of his body down the shaft of an abandoned gold mine, where it remained for nearly 40 years. The defendant, Alice Uden, wore wire-rimmed glasses, a court-supplied hearing aid, and a blue suit, and sat quietly in her wheelchair before addressing the court. She sobbed gently as she spoke to the court about the death of her third husband, Ronald Holtz, who was 25 at the time. 'I've tried to atone for it,' Uden said. 'I wish I had never met him, so none of this would have ever happened. He was a very frightening man.' Jurors in Cheyenne didn't accept Uden's argument that she shot Holtz in the head to protect her toddler daughter from him. In May, they found her guilty of second-degree murder. Uden killed Holtz in late 1974 or early 1975 in Cheyenne, where he was living with her and her two-year-old daughter. Uden testified that she shot him with a rifle after he became enraged over the girl's crying and was about to attack her in bed. Laramie County District Court Judge Steven Sharpe stated that he considered possible mitigating factors, including Uden's lack of a prior criminal record. 'This was very much a cold, calculated murder,' Sharpe said. 'The jury heard all the evidence presented and rejected the defense of self-defense.' District Attorney Scott Homar argued that the killing was a deliberate act that rid Uden of Holtz. 'Her way out was to take Mr. Holtz's life while he was sleeping and then dispose of the body in a way that it wouldn't be found for 39 1/2 years,' Homar said. Police arrested Uden and her fourth and current husband, Gerald Uden, 72, both of Chadwick, Missouri, last fall in southwest Missouri, accusing them of murdering former spouses in separate incidents. Gerald Uden has pleaded guilty to killing his ex-wife and her two sons in central Wyoming in 1980. Prosecutors have not established any link between the two cases. At her trial, Alice Uden testified that she removed Christmas decorations from a large cardboard barrel and placed Holtz's body inside. She wrestled the barrel into her trunk, she said, and dumped it into an abandoned gold mine on a ranch between Cheyenne and Laramie. One of Uden's sons, Todd Scott, testified at the trial that his mother told him decades ago that she had shot Holtz while he was asleep. After previous, unsuccessful attempts to locate Holtz's remains in the mine, which was filled with the carcasses of cattle and other ranch animals, investigators dug deeper into the vertical shaft last summer and finally unearthed Holtz's remains. Evidence presented to the court included a returned envelope containing divorce papers initiated by Alice Uden against the husband she murdered after only a few months together. The jury did not find Uden guilty of premeditated, first-degree murder, which would have carried a mandatory life sentence. The jury also declined to convict her of a less-serious charge of manslaughter. Uden's attorney, Donald Miller, urged the judge to sentence Uden to probation because her now-adult daughter, Erica Prunty, has cancer and has been given six months to live. He also highlighted Holtz's psychiatric history, stating he met Uden, a former nurse, while she was working in the psychiatric unit at a Veterans Administration hospital in Sheridan. 'His behavior was unpredictable. He was irritable, he was hostile, he was explosive. He had no incentive to change,' Miller told the courtroom. Prosecutors in the case against Gerald Uden said that the bodies of 32-year-old Virginia Uden, and her two sons, 11-year-old Richard Uden and 10-year-old Reagan Uden, have not yet been found. Gerald Uden told a Fremont County courtroom in November that he shot each of them with a rifle not far from his home, one after the other, and dumped their bodies in an abandoned mine. Months later, he said, he retrieved the bodies and sank them in Fremont Lake in western Wyoming. Investigators briefly searched the deep lake for the bodies and say they plan a more comprehensive search soon. Jurors at Alice Uden's trial were not allowed to hear about Gerald Uden's case.
translated_content: Sutkinja u Wyomingu osudila je u ponedjeljak 75-godišnju ženu iz Missourija na doživotni zatvor zbog ubistva njenog supruga puškom sredinom 1970-ih i bacanja njegovog tijela u šaht napuštenog rudnika zlata, gdje je ostalo gotovo 40 godina. Optužena, Alice Uden, nosila je naočale s metalnim okvirom, slušni aparat koji joj je osigurao sud i plavo odijelo, te je tiho sjedila u invalidskim kolicima prije nego što se obratila sudu. Nježno je jecala dok je govorila sudu o smrti svog trećeg supruga, Ronalda Holtza, koji je tada imao 25 godina. ’Pokušala sam se iskupiti za to,’ rekla je Uden. ’Voljela bih da ga nikada nisam upoznala, tako da se ništa od ovoga ne bi dogodilo. Bio je vrlo zastrašujući čovjek.’ Porotnici u Cheyenneu nisu prihvatili Udenin argument da je upucala Holtza u glavu kako bi zaštitila svoju kćerku. U maju su je proglasili krivom za ubistvo drugog stepena. Uden je ubila Holtza krajem 1974. ili početkom 1975. u Cheyenneu, gdje je živio s njom i njenom dvogodišnjom kćerkom. Uden je svjedočila da ga je upucala puškom nakon što je pobjesnio zbog kćerkinog plača i umalo je napao u krevetu. Sutkinja Okružnog suda Laramie County, Steven Sharpe, izjavio je da je razmotrio moguće olakšavajuće okolnosti, uključujući Udenin nedostatak prethodne krivične evidencije. ’Ovo je bilo vrlo hladno, proračunato ubistvo,’ rekao je Sharpe. ’Porota je čula sve izvedene dokaze i odbacila odbranu da je to bila samoodbrana.’ Okružni tužilac Scott Homar tvrdio je da je ubistvo bio namjeran čin koji je oslobodio Uden od Holtza. ’Njen izlaz je bio da oduzme život g. Holtzu dok je spavao i zatim odloži tijelo na način da ga se ne pronađe 39 i po godina,’ rekao je Homar. Policija je uhapsila Uden i njenog četvrtog i sadašnjeg supruga, Geralda Udena (72), oboje iz Chadwicka u Missouriju, prošle jeseni u jugozapadnom Missouriju, optužujući ih da su ubili bivše supružnike u odvojenim slučajevima. Gerald Uden se izjasnio krivim za ubistvo svoje bivše žene i njena dva sina u centralnom Wyomingu 1980. godine. Tužioci nisu utvrdili nikakvu vezu između ova dva slučaja. Na suđenju je Alice Uden svjedočila da je uklonila božićne ukrase iz velike kartonske bačve i stavila Holtzovo tijelo unutra. Rekla je da je ugurala bačvu u svoj prtljažnik i bacila je u napušteni rudnik zlata na ranču između Cheyennea i Laramieja. Jedan od Udeninih sinova, Todd Scott, svjedočio je na suđenju da mu je majka prije desetljeća rekla da je upucala Holtza dok je spavao. Nakon prethodnih, neuspješnih pokušaja da pronađu Holtzove ostatke u rudniku, koji je bio ispunjen leševima stoke i drugih životinja s ranča, istražitelji su prošlog ljeta iskopali dublje u vertikalni šaht i konačno iskopali Holtzove ostatke. Kao dokaz sudu je predočena vraćena koverta koja je sadržavala papire za razvod koje je pokrenula Alice Uden protiv supruga kojeg je ubila nakon samo nekoliko mjeseci braka. Porota nije proglasila Uden krivom za ubistvo s predumišljajem prvog stepena, što bi povlačilo obaveznu doživotnu kaznu. Porota je također odbila da je osudi za manje tešku optužbu za ubistvo iz nehata. Udenin advokat, Donald Miller, pozvao je sutkinju da osudi Uden na uvjetnu kaznu jer njena sada odrasla kćerka, Erica Prunty, ima rak i predviđeno joj je šest mjeseci života. Također je istakao Holtzovu psihijatrijsku historiju, navodeći da je upoznao Uden, bivšu medicinsku sestru, dok je radila na psihijatrijskom odjelu u bolnici za veterane u Sheridanu. ’Njegovo ponašanje je bilo nepredvidivo. Bio je razdražljiv, neprijateljski raspoložen, eksplozivan. Nije imao poticaja da se promijeni,’ rekao je Miller u sudnici. Tužioci u slučaju protiv Geralda Udena rekli su da tijela 32-godišnje Virginije Uden, i njena dva sina, 11-godišnjeg Richarda Udena i 10-godišnjeg Reagana Udena, još uvijek nisu pronađena. Gerald Uden je u novembru rekao u sudnici okruga Fremont da ih je sve upucao puškom nedaleko od svoje kuće, jednog za drugim, i bacio njihova tijela u napušteni rudnik. Mjesecima kasnije, rekao je, izvukao je tijela i potopio ih u jezero Fremont u zapadnom Wyomingu. Istražitelji su nakratko pretražili duboko jezero u potrazi za tijelima i kažu da uskoro planiraju opsežniju pretragu. Porotnicima na suđenju Alice Uden nije bilo dopušteno da čuju za slučaj Geralda Udena.

A passenger and her pig were escorted off a US Airways flight after the animal began defecating on the floor and squealing loudly, according to a fellow traveler. Rob Phelps reported the incident to Mail Online, stating he was flying from Hartford, Connecticut, to Washington's Reagan Airport for Thanksgiving on Wednesday morning when he observed the animal being brought onto the cabin on a leash.

Phelps, 65, described the 80-pound pig as screaming 'three times louder than a child' as its owner guided it down the aisle, struggling to walk independently. 'It was ridiculous,' he recounted. 'It started to smell, and flight attendants instructed her to clean up the mess.'

Phelps, 63, who was traveling with his wife, noted that passengers began complaining after five or ten minutes as the pig became increasingly agitated. He overheard the woman talking to the pig as if it were a person, even calling it a 'jerk' for its behavior. She had been permitted to bring it onboard as an 'emotional support' animal, based on Department of Transportation guidelines.

Airline staff determined the situation was untenable, and the woman and her animal were removed from the cabin. Phelps mentioned that passengers were silent with a mixture of laughter and shock when they first saw the pig. 'You couldn't write this,' he said. 'I have seen dogs and cats in cages on a plane - but never a pig.' He emphasized the pig's size, saying, 'This was not a small pig. When she held it over her shoulder it reached her waist.' He questioned how the animal cleared security: 'I don't even know how it got through. You have the TSA and intense security, and yet it still was let on board.'

Phelps said the pig was the primary topic of conversation for the rest of the flight, and he was still amused by it on Thanksgiving Day. American Airlines, the parent company of US Airways, confirmed the woman had the pig as an emotional support animal and was asked to leave due to its disruptive behavior.

In 2012, the Department of Transportation issued guidelines allowing certain animals, including pot-bellied pigs, to be designated as 'Emotional Support' animals, alongside monkeys and miniature horses. Transportation officers assess whether an animal meets the criteria for travel based on these guidelines. Pigs are sometimes favored as service animals for individuals with dog allergies, being considered intelligent and attuned to dangerous situations.

article_content: Lucian Freud's purported 'first son' has been unsuccessful in his attempt to claim a portion of the artist's £96 million fortune, following a High Court dispute. Paul McAdam Freud is acknowledged, though not definitively proven, to be Freud's son from a relationship with Katherine McAdam in the 1950s. Mr. McAdam Freud, brother of fashion designer Bella Freud, contested a clause in his father's will that excluded him from any inheritance. He also challenged a provision that restricts knowledge of the estate's ultimate beneficiaries to only two individuals. Paul McAdam Freud (left), the alleged 'secret son' of the elusive artist Lucian Freud (right), lost his High Court bid to uncover the beneficiaries of Freud's will and potentially secure a share. Upon Freud's death three years ago, Diana Rawstrom, his trusted solicitor, and Rose Pearce, one of his daughters, were the sole initial inheritors. After accounting for legacies and taxes, they inherited approximately £42 million. However, they later disclosed that Freud had secretly instructed them to distribute money to a list of others, without revealing their identities or the amounts involved. Mr. McAdam Freud sought to break this secrecy by arguing that a portion of the will was invalid, but his challenge was rejected. Had he succeeded, Freud would have been considered largely intestate, and his assets would have been distributed to his next of kin, a complex task given the uncertain number of his children – cited in court as 'at least 14'. Lucian's only acknowledged legitimate children, daughters Annie and Annabel, resulted from his marriage to Kitty Garman, his muse whom he married in 1948. However, he fathered four children with Suzy Boyt, a student he met at the Slade School of Art in the Fifties, and another four, including Paul McAdam Freud and sisters Jane, Bella, and Esther, with Kathleen McAdam. Following Kathleen's departure in 1966, it is reported that he had minimal contact with the family for two decades. Greek sculptor Vassilakis Takis, a close associate of Lucian's, estimated that he had at least 500 lovers during his lifetime, while family friends suggest his children could number as many as 30. Revealing the actual beneficiaries of Freud's will could have shed light on some of the mystery, but the recent ruling ensures that only Mrs. Rawstrom and Mrs. Pearce will know who receives the funds. Speaking at the High Court, the judge stated that he could ‘readily understand’ Mr. MacAdam Freud’s concerns regarding the will's secrecy, from which he was excluded. ‘There is a lot of money involved here, so I fully understand these are important issues,’ he commented, before concluding that Mrs. Rawstrom’s and Mrs. Pearce’s interpretation of the will was reasonable. Freud amassed his fortune through his portraiture, considered by many to be among the finest of his era. His most renowned work, 'Benefits Supervisor Sleeping' (pictured), achieved a world-record price of $33.8 million in 2008. Freud's portraits frequently featured nudes of his friends and family. This particular portrait depicts his daughter, Bella. Although the will initially appeared to grant the £42 million to Mrs. Rawstrom and Mrs. Pearce ‘absolutely’, they have clarified that they hold the funds as trustees and are obligated to distribute them confidentially. ‘They wish to respect the deceased’s wishes not to disclose the terms of the fully secret trust to anyone who is not a beneficiary,’ their barrister, Michael Furness QC, stated to the court. The judge noted that Mr. McAdam Freud's paternity had ‘at one time been disputed’ but was accepted for the hearing's purposes, acknowledging him as ‘another of Lucian Freud’s children’ from his relationship with fashion student, Katherine McAdam, in the 1950s. The artist's will specifically provided a £2.5 million tax-free gift and a house in west London to his assistant of over 20 years, David Dawson. A further clause directed Mrs. Pearce and Mrs. Rawstron to dispose of ‘chattels’ according to instructions given during Freud's lifetime. One of Freud’s works was also donated to the National Gallery in lieu of inheritance tax.

Lucianova jedina priznata zakonita djeca, kćeri Annie i Annabel, proizašle su iz njegovog braka sa Kitty Garman, njegovom muzom kojom se oženio 1948. Međutim, dobio je četvero djece sa Suzy Boyt, studenticom koju je upoznao u Školi umjetnosti Slade 1950-ih, i još četvero, uključujući Paula McAdama Freuda i sestre Jane, Bellu i Esther, sa Kathleen McAdam. Grčki kipar Vassilakis Takis, bliski saradnik Luciana, procijenio je da je imao najmanje 500 ljubavnika tokom svog života, dok prijatelji porodice sugeriraju da bi broj njegove djece mogao biti čak 30. Otkrivanje stvarnih korisnika Freudovog testamenta moglo je rasvijetliti dio misterije, ali nedavna presuda osigurava da će samo gospođa Rawstrom i gospođa Pearce znati ko prima sredstva. Govoreći na Visokom sudu, sudija je izjavio da može 'lako razumjeti' zabrinutost gospodina MacAdama Freuda u vezi s tajnovitošću testamenta, iz kojeg je bio isključen. ‘Uključeno je puno novca, tako da u potpunosti razumijem da su ovo važna pitanja’, komentirao je, prije nego što je zaključio da je tumačenje testamenta gospođe Rawstrom i gospođe Pearce razumno. Freud je stekao svoje bogatstvo kroz portretiranje, koje mnogi smatraju jednim od najboljih svog doba. Njegovo najpoznatije djelo, 'Benefits Supervisor Sleeping' (na slici), postiglo je svjetski rekordnu cijenu od 33,8 miliona dolara 2008. Freudovi portreti su često prikazivali aktove njegovih prijatelja i porodice. Ovaj određeni portret prikazuje njegovu kćer, Bellu. Sudija je primijetio da je očinstvo gospodina McAdama Freuda 'u jednom trenutku bilo sporno', ali je prihvaćeno u svrhu saslušanja, priznavši ga kao 'još jedno od djece Luciana Freuda' iz njegove veze sa studenticom mode, Katherine McAdam, 1950-ih. Umjetnikov testament je posebno predviđao poklon od 2,5 miliona funti oslobođen poreza i kuću u zapadnom Londonu njegovom asistentu više od 20 godina, Davidu Dawsonu. Daljnja klauzula je naložila gospođi Pearce i gospođi Rawstron da raspolažu 'pokretninama' prema uputama datim tokom Freudovog života. article_content: A customer was asked to leave a Seattle restaurant for refusing to remove his Google Glass. Nick Starr was at the Lost Lake Cafe in Seattle on November 21, wearing Google Glass, which allows users to take pictures and record audio or video. He was asked to remove them. He refused and was eventually asked to leave, sparking an online dispute between Starr and the restaurant and raising questions about how invasive the gadget is. Starr complained about the incident on his Facebook page, explaining that he and his boyfriend were at the cafe looking at the menus when a manager approached them, KIRO reported. Scroll down for video Dispute: Nick Starr left a Seattle restaurant after he was ordered to remove his Google Glass, pictured. 'She told me that the owner's other restaurant doesn't allow Google Glass and that I would have to either put it away or leave,' he wrote. 'I asked to see where it was policy for Glass to be disallowed at Lost Lake. She said she couldn't provide any and when asked to speak with management she stated she was the night manager.' Refusing to remove the glasses, Starr and his boyfriend left. He vented on his Facebook post, demanding an apology from the restaurant and calling for the woman's termination. He added that he thought it was bizarre that the restaurant asked customers to share images on social networking sites of their experiences there but banned Google Glass. Scene: The manager at the Lost Lake Cafe asked him to remove the glasses in accordance with their policy. Anger: Restaurant owner David Meinert, pictured, said he thought the glasses were invasive. But the Lost Lake Cafe has refused to apologize, stating that they have other customers' interests in mind. They responded to Starr with their own Facebook post, outlining its policy. 'We recently had to ask a rude customer to leave because of their insistence on wearing and operating Google Glass inside the restaurant,' the statement said. 'We kindly ask our customers to refrain from wearing and operating Google Glass inside Lost Lake. We also ask that you not videotape anyone using any other sort of technology.' 'If you do wear your Google Glass inside, or film or photograph people without their permission, you will be asked to stop or leave. And if we ask you to leave, for God's sake, don't start yelling about your "rights". Just shut up and get out before you make things worse.' Night out: Starr was out with his boyfriend, Brian (left), when they were approached by the manager. Fan: Starr said he wears the glasses everywhere and argued you can also take pictures with cell phones. Owner David Meinert, who banned Google Glass at another one of his restaurants earlier this year, said he felt uneasy about the device. 'I think they're invasive and they make people uncomfortable,' he told KOMO News. 'More than that they make me uncomfortable, and it's my place.' But Starr countered that he believes Google Glass is no more intrusive than cell phones with cameras that are also capable of taking images. 'I think privacy is vapor now,' Starr said. 'There are cameras everywhere. There are recording devices everywhere.' See below for video

article_content: According to a prominent bookstore, children are returning to the types of books enjoyed by their grandparents. A new generation of authors, inspired by classic writers such as Enid Blyton, has spearheaded the resurgence of mystery and detective novels for young readers. The Waterstones Children’s Book Prize shortlist features six novels centered around resourceful children solving mysteries independently, echoing beloved series like Nancy Drew, the Hardy Boys, and Enid Blyton’s Famous Five. The shortlist for the Waterstones Children’s Book Prize suggests that children are now engaging with literature similar to what their grandparents read. Half of the shortlisted novels in the ‘Best Books for Teens’ and ‘Best Fiction for 5-12s’ categories are mystery stories. In recent years, teenage reading lists have been dominated by vampire novels and dystopian narratives, while light-hearted ‘funny fiction’ has been popular among younger readers. However, current trends indicate a demand for wholesome novels that resonate with parents' childhood memories. Notable books nominated for the prize include ‘Murder Most Unladylike’ by Robin Stevens, which follows two boarding school students investigating their teacher's murder, and ‘Smart’ by Kim Slater, focusing on a teen outsider exploring the death of a homeless man. Melissa Cox, head of children’s buying at Waterstones, noted, ‘Crime fiction is a consistently popular genre for adults, but the recent revival of children’s mystery books is particularly noteworthy.’ ‘Enid Blyton is a quintessential children’s mystery author, and her storytelling has clearly influenced several of our shortlisted authors. Classic series like The Famous Five are informing successful contemporary children's books.’ ‘This trend is a return to more traditional storytelling compared to the prevalence of funny fiction for younger audiences or dystopian and vampire fiction for teenagers.’ ‘Books that parents consider something they would have enjoyed in their own childhoods are often easier to promote.’ ‘By drawing from the detective genre, many of our shortlisted authors have enabled their characters to address significant issues within a secure and familiar context for young readers.’ ‘However, some books have simply captured the classic enjoyment of apprehending the villain.’ ‘Girl Online,’ the popular novel by YouTube personality Zoella (Zoe Sugg), also reflects a desire for ‘innocent’ books aimed at tweens and teens. Ms. Cox added, ‘Zoella’s book is very clean. There is nothing in it that parents would find alarming.’ Natalie Doherty, from Penguin Random House and editor of ‘Murder Most Unladylike,’ which is shortlisted in the Best Fiction for 5-12 category, stated that the novel offers a modern twist on two classic children’s genres. She explained, ‘It combines the traditional murder mystery story in the style of Agatha Christie with the Enid Blyton-style boarding school stories like Mallory Towers.’ ‘It offers a nostalgic appeal to those who grew up reading these types of novels.’ ‘Despite this, it doesn’t feel dated. It is fresh and modern and addresses themes like racism, same-sex relationships, and bullying.’ ‘It’s also very humorous, with plenty of dry wit.’ The winner of the Waterstones Children’s Book Prize will be announced on March 26. Six books will compete in each category: Best Illustrated Book, Best Fiction for 5-12s, and Best Books for Teens. The winning author in each category will receive £2,000, with the overall winner receiving an additional £3,000. Mystery novels nominated for Best Fiction for 5-12s include ‘Murder Most Unladylike’ by Robin Stevens, ‘Violet and the Pearl of the Orient’ by Harriet Whitehorn, and ‘A Boy Called Hope’ by Lara Williamson. Shortlisted mystery novels in the Best Books for Teens category include ‘The Apple Tart of Hope’ by Sarah Moore Fitzgerald, ‘Dead Ends’ by Erin Lange, and ‘Smart’ by Kim Slater.

article_content: Recent paleontological explorations in the Tatacoa Desert in Colombia led to the recovery of the most complete skeleton of a 'saber-toothed marsupial' discovered in northern South America. The specimen belongs to the species Anachlysictis gracilis, a member of the extinct predatory mammal group known as sparassodonts, which lived in South America during the Cenozoic Era, after the extinction of the dinosaurs. This species lived approximately 13 million years ago in the area known among paleontologists as 'La Venta,' located in the current La Tatacoa desert, which was then a tropical rainforest, similar to the Amazon today, according to Dr. Catalina Suarez, a Swiss National Science Foundation fellow working at the Argentine Institute of Nivology, Glaciology and Environmental Sciences, who led the analysis of the remains and the publication of their results in the journal Geodiversitas. Prior to this finding, only a fragment of a mandible and a few other remains had been found for this species, which is related to living marsupials such as kangaroos, koalas, and opossums. Before its extinction, A. gracilis was one of several terrestrial carnivores in South America, similar to pumas, wildcats, and foxes that currently inhabit the continent. 'Thanks to this discovery, we were able to learn new details about this fascinating species,' said Suarez. 'The analyses allowed us to understand what these extinct predators were like and how they lived in Neotropical South America millions of years ago.' The three species of the family Thylacosmilidae on the South American continent: Anachlysictis gracilis (left, above), Thylacosmilus atrox (right) and Patagosmilus goini (left, below). Credit: Artist: Jorge Blanco Suarez began her research on A. gracilis in the laboratory of paleontologist Carlos Jaramillo at the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute, where she was an intern and a pre- and post-doctoral fellow. She is now a specialist in metatherians, the group that includes marsupials and their extinct relatives, such as the family Thylacosmilidae, to which the fossil of A. gracilis belongs. The most distinctive feature of this family is their curved and flattened canines, resembling sabers, hence their common name 'saber-toothed marsupials.' 'Our research confirms that this Colombian fossil 'saber-tooth marsupial' A. gracilis is closely related to Thylacosmilus, the most widely recognized 'saber-tooth marsupial,' said Dr. Javier Luque, a former STRI fellow, co-author of the study and senior research associate at the University of Cambridge Museum of Zoology. 'Both groups, along with Patagosmilus (another of these 'saber-tooth marsupials'), form their own family, Thylacosmilidae, in the mammal tree of life. This family is characterized by its long and enormously curved, saber-shaped upper canines, and by an extension of the anterior part of the jaw that resembles a sheath for these 'sabers.' By analyzing the molar teeth, tooth shape, and mandible of the remains, it was possible to determine the approximate weight and diet of A. gracilis. The results revealed that it weighed on average about 23 kg (like a lynx) and was a hypercarnivore, meaning it ate mainly meat. Its potential prey would have included small mammals that inhabited the area, such as marsupials, spiny rats, porcupines, rodents of various sizes, and even primates, which were very abundant in the region. 'In a future study, we will address all the other bones in its body, which include various sections of the spine, ribs, hip, scapulae—what we call 'shoulder blades' for humans— and bones in its legs,' Suarez said. 'This will allow us to explore aspects of how it moved, the position in which its neck held its head, whether it was a runner, whether it could climb, whether its hands could hold objects more easily, as many marsupials do when feeding, or whether it was a bit more difficult, as it is for example for a dog or a cat.' The new fossil of A. gracilis is housed in the La Tatacoa Natural History Museum, in the town of La Victoria in the municipality of Villavieja (department of Huila, Colombia), along with other surprising finds that have been unearthed in one of the most amazing places on the continent. Current landscape in one of the fossiliferous localities of the La Tatacoa desert. Credit: Catalina Suarez 'The fossil specimen of A. gracilis that we describe in this research constitutes an iconic fossil because of its excellent preservation, three-dimensionality, and importance for understanding the paleobiological aspects of this predatory marsupial that roamed the forests of northern South America approximately 13 million years ago,' added Dr. Edwin Cadena, researcher at Universidad del Rosario and STRI, and co-author of the study. 'With this finding, we show the importance of continuing to support paleontological scientific activity in the Neotropics, in order to be able to make new discoveries that will help us understand the evolutionary history and paleobiodiversity of this part of the continent.'
translated_content: Nedavna paleontološka istraživanja u pustinji Tatacoa u Kolumbiji dovela su do otkrića najkompletnijeg skeleta 'torbarskog sabljastog zuba' pronađenog u sjevernom dijelu Južne Amerike. Primjerak pripada vrsti Anachlysictis gracilis, članu izumrle skupine grabežljivih sisavaca poznatih kao sparassodonti, koji su živjeli u Južnoj Americi tijekom kenozoika, nakon izumiranja dinosaura. Ova vrsta je živjela prije otprilike 13 milijuna godina na području poznatom među paleontolozima kao 'La Venta', smještenom u današnjoj pustinji La Tatacoa, koja je tada bila tropska prašuma, slična današnjoj Amazoni, prema riječima dr. Cataline Suarez, stipendistice Švicarske nacionalne zaklade za znanost koja radi na Argentinskom institutu za nivologiju, glaciologiju i znanosti o okolišu, koja je vodila analizu ostataka i objavu rezultata u časopisu Geodiversitas. Prije ovog otkrića, pronađen je samo fragment mandibule i nekoliko drugih ostataka ove vrste, koja je srodna živućim torbarima kao što su klokani, koale i oposumi. Prije svog izumiranja, A. gracilis je bio jedan od nekoliko kopnenih mesoždera u Južnoj Americi, sličan pumama, divljim mačkama i lisicama koje danas nastanjuju kontinent. 'Zahvaljujući ovom otkriću, uspjeli smo naučiti nove detalje o ovoj fascinantnoj vrsti', rekla je Suarez. 'Analize su nam omogućile da razumijemo kakvi su bili ovi izumrli grabežljivci i kako su živjeli u neotropskoj Južnoj Americi prije milijuna godina.' Tri vrste porodice Thylacosmilidae na južnoameričkom kontinentu: Anachlysictis gracilis (lijevo, gore), Thylacosmilus atrox (desno) i Patagosmilus goini (lijevo, dolje). Zasluge: Umjetnik: Jorge Blanco Suarez je započela svoje istraživanje o A. gracilis u laboratoriju paleontologa Carlosa Jaramilla na Institutu za tropska istraživanja Smithsonian, gdje je bila stažistica te preddoktorska i poslijedoktorska stipendistica. Sada je specijalistica za metaterije, skupinu koja uključuje torbare i njihove izumrle srodnike, poput porodice Thylacosmilidae, kojoj pripada fosil A. gracilis. Najistaknutija značajka ove porodice su njihovi zakrivljeni i spljošteni očnjaci, koji podsjećaju na sablje, pa su stoga poznati kao 'torbarski sabljasti zubi'. 'Naše istraživanje potvrđuje da je ovaj kolumbijski fosil 'torbarskog sabljastog zuba' A. gracilis usko povezan s Thylacosmilusom, najpoznatijim 'torbarskim sabljastim zubom'', rekao je dr. Javier Luque, bivši stipendist STRI-a, koautor studije i viši znanstveni suradnik u Zoološkom muzeju Sveučilišta u Cambridgeu. 'Obje skupine, zajedno s Patagosmilusom (još jednim od ovih 'torbarskih sabljastih zuba'), čine vlastitu porodicu, Thylacosmilidae, u stablu života sisavaca. Ovu porodicu karakteriziraju dugi i iznimno zakrivljeni gornji očnjaci u obliku sablje, te produžetak prednjeg dijela čeljusti koji podsjeća na korice za te 'sablje'. Analizom kutnjaka, oblika zuba i mandibule ostataka, bilo je moguće utvrditi približnu težinu i prehranu vrste A. gracilis. Rezultati su otkrili da je u prosjeku težio oko 23 kg (kao ris) i bio je hipermesojed, što znači da je jeo uglavnom meso. Njegov potencijalni plijen uključivao bi male sisavce koji su nastanjivali to područje, kao što su torbari, bodljikavi štakori, dikobrazi, glodavci različitih veličina, pa čak i primati, koji su bili vrlo brojni u regiji. 'U budućoj studiji pozabavit ćemo se svim ostalim kostima u njegovom tijelu, koje uključuju različite dijelove kralježnice, rebara, kuka, lopatica - što za ljude zovemo 'ramena' - i kostima u njegovim nogama', rekla je Suarez. 'To će nam omogućiti da istražimo aspekte kako se kretao, položaj u kojem je njegov vrat držao glavu, je li bio trkač, je li se mogao penjati, mogu li njegove ruke lakše držati predmete, kao što to mnogi torbari čine prilikom hranjenja, ili je li to bilo malo teže, kao što je to primjerice psu ili mački.' Novi fosil A. gracilis nalazi se u Prirodoslovnom muzeju La Tatacoa, u gradu La Victoria u općini Villavieja (departman Huila, Kolumbija), zajedno s drugim iznenađujućim nalazima koji su iskopani na jednom od najnevjerojatnijih mjesta na kontinentu. Trenutni krajolik u jednom od lokaliteta s fosilima u pustinji La Tatacoa. Zasluge: Catalina Suarez 'Fosilni primjerak A. gracilisa koji opisujemo u ovom istraživanju predstavlja ikonski fosil zbog svoje izvrsne očuvanosti, trodimenzionalnosti i važnosti za razumijevanje paleobioloških aspekata ovog grabežljivog torbara koji je lutao šumama sjeverne Južne Amerike prije otprilike 13 milijuna godina', dodao je dr. Edwin Cadena, istraživač na Universidad del Rosario i STRI, i koautor studije. 'Ovim nalazom pokazujemo važnost nastavka podrške paleontološkoj znanstvenoj aktivnosti u neotropima, kako bismo mogli doći do novih otkrića koja će nam pomoći razumjeti evolucijsku povijest i paleobioraznolikost ovog dijela kontinenta.'

The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge are set to move into their newly renovated home at Kensington Palace, following a £1.5 million refurbishment. This elegant 20-room apartment, filled with priceless antiques from the Royal Collection, will serve as both the couple's primary residence and a family home for Prince George. The decor, described as 'Style Anglaise,' blends classic English country house aesthetics with a modern touch.

This contrasts sharply with their previous, more modest four-bedroom farmhouse on Anglesey, which William and Kate left after the prince concluded his service as a Search and Rescue pilot. While residing on Anglesey, Kate frequented the Homebase DIY store on the Penrhos Industrial Estate in Holyhead. Staff members recall her spending considerable time browsing, particularly in the lighting and bathroom sections, often purchasing small items for her home. Purchases included a £22.99 three-tier chocolate brown 'faux leather' letter tray, a £12.99 cork memo board, and a £10.99 faux leather magazine file.

The Kensington Palace apartment, known as Apartment 1A, was formerly the residence of Princess Margaret. This spacious four-story property features five reception rooms, three main bedrooms, nurseries, staff quarters, and a large south-facing walled garden designed by Sir Christopher Wren.

The renovation, while funded partially by the Royal Family, has also utilized public funds. Structural work, rewiring, the installation of new environmentally-friendly heating and hot water systems, and asbestos removal are being covered by the government, while William and Kate are personally paying for decoration and furnishings. The discovery of asbestos and necessary roof repairs have contributed to the rising costs. Kate is selecting antiques from the Royal Collection to furnish the apartment. She is overseeing the design work herself, with encouragement from Prince Charles, focusing on British-sourced, environmentally-friendly products.

article_content: The pensions minister warned that stay-at-home mothers should fight for a share of their ex-husband’s pension when they divorce, or risk financial hardship in retirement. Steve Webb stated that valuable workplace pensions are often not given enough importance when couples negotiate their divorce settlements. This means many divorcees, particularly women who have taken career breaks to care for children, may face relying on the State pension in old age. Divorced mothers have been advised to seek a portion of their ex-husband's pensions to avoid potential financial loss later in life, especially if they interrupted their careers to raise children. Mr. Webb suggested that divorce lawyers should be ‘encouraged to always ensure this is properly part of the negotiations and is on the table’. The Liberal Democrat MP noted that workplace pensions were frequently ‘an afterthought’ and urged people not to underestimate their worth. He said: ‘If you are part of a couple and you do not contribute to a pension for family reasons – whether that is caring for children or family members – and then you separate close to retirement, there is a potential risk there. ‘It is tempting to prioritize immediate needs like the house and children, but it is crucial to ensure that the pension sharing issue is at the forefront. ‘There is a risk that the pension becomes an afterthought and that people think ‘I will worry about that at retirement’. However, a pension, especially a final salary pension, is very valuable, and that future value is not always easy to understand’. Earlier that day, he addressed the issue at a conference hosted by the Resolution Foundation think tank, stating that the impact of divorce on pension income was ‘one of the elephants in the room’. Pensions Minister Steve Webb said that pensions were often seen as 'an afterthought' in divorce. He said: ‘We have a problem with divorce. Many people – particularly women – take career breaks or take time off to have children and then return to work having missed out [on pension contributions]. ‘If a couple remains together in retirement then they are financially secure between them, but what if they separate in their fifties?’. Approximately four in 10 marriages in the UK now end in divorce, according to official statistics. Pensions are often a couple’s largest asset in a divorce after the family home, and they can be split or shared in several ways. Court agreements can be obtained for ‘pension sharing’, which involves transferring a percentage share of the pension to the ex-partner. Alternatively, people can offset the pension against other assets – for example, one partner may receive a larger share of the family home in exchange for the other keeping their pension. Others agree to receive a deferred lump sum when their partner retires. Mr. Webb acknowledged that there were no ‘quick fixes’ for the problem but advocated for increased awareness among divorcees regarding the future value of pensions. He said: ‘In theory, we have pension sharing on divorce and pension splitting. ‘However, the reality is that it doesn’t work very well. Your average divorce lawyer is focused on the house and, if you still have children, are you really going to strongly negotiate over a share of the pension?’. Family lawyer Marilyn Stowe stated that the lower-earning spouse was often given immediate capital, such as the house or a lump sum, while longer-term assets like pensions were often ‘left in the hands of the other party’. She said: ‘I agree that the long-term needs should never be ignored, but circumstances tend to prioritize immediate needs.’ Mrs. Stowe said that law firms and courts would ‘never forget such a valuable asset’ in negotiations, but couples who reached an informal agreement could make mistakes. She added: ‘With legal aid no longer available for divorce, many couples may think they cannot afford a lawyer and could overlook the value of pensions.’ Caroline Abrahams, of Age UK, said: ‘It’s important that everyone is encouraged to save money for later life. ‘Age UK believes older people should be offered periodic ‘financial MOTs’ so that they know how financially secure they are. That includes understanding, if you are part of a couple, what happens to your pension when your partner dies or if your situation changes for other reasons.’
translated_content: Ministar za penzije upozorio je da bi se majke koje ne rade trebale boriti za udio u penziji svog bivšeg muža prilikom razvoda, inače riskiraju finansijske poteškoće u starosti. Steve Webb je izjavio da se vrijednim penzijama s radnog mjesta često ne pridaje dovoljno važnosti kada parovi pregovaraju o podjeli imovine prilikom razvoda. To znači da se mnogi razvedeni, a posebno žene koje su napravile pauzu u karijeri kako bi se brinule o djeci, mogu suočiti s oslanjanjem na državnu penziju u starosti. Razvedenim majkama se savjetuje da traže dio penzije svojih bivših muževa kako bi izbjegle potencijalni finansijski gubitak u budućnosti, pogotovo ako su prekinule karijeru da bi odgajale djecu. Gospodin Webb je predložio da bi advokati za razvode trebali biti 'ohrabreni da osiguraju da je pitanje penzije uvijek dio pregovora i na stolu'. Liberalni demokratski poslanik je primijetio da su penzije s radnog mjesta često 'naknadna misao' i pozvao je ljude da ne podcjenjuju njihovu vrijednost. Rekao je: 'Ako ste u braku i ne uplaćujete u penzioni fond iz porodičnih razloga – bilo da se radi o brizi za djecu ili starije članove porodice – a zatim se rastanete pred penziju, postoji potencijalni rizik. ‘Primamljivo je dati prednost trenutnim potrebama poput kuće i djece, ali ključno je osigurati da je pitanje podjele penzije prioritet. ‘Postoji rizik da penzija postane naknadna misao i da ljudi misle 'Brinut ću o tome kad odem u penziju'. Međutim, penzija, posebno ona sa zagarantovanom platom, vrlo je vrijedna, a tu buduću vrijednost nije uvijek lako shvatiti’. Ranije tog dana, govorio je o ovom problemu na konferenciji koju je organizovao institut Resolution Foundation, navodeći da je uticaj razvoda na penzioni prihod 'jedan od najvećih problema'. Ministar za penzije Steve Webb je rekao da se penzije često vide kao 'naknadna misao' prilikom razvoda. Rekao je: ‘Razvod je problem. Mnogi ljudi – posebno žene – prave pauze u karijeri ili odsustvuju s posla da bi imali djecu, a zatim se vraćaju na posao propustivši priliku za doprinose u penzioni fond. ‘Ako par ostane zajedno do penzije, onda su finansijski sigurni, ali šta ako se rastanu u pedesetim?’. Otprilike četiri od 10 brakova u Velikoj Britaniji sada završe razvodom, prema službenoj statistici. Penzije su često najveća imovina para prilikom razvoda, odmah nakon porodične kuće, i mogu se podijeliti na nekoliko načina. Sudski sporazumi se mogu postići za 'podjelu penzije', što uključuje prenos procentualnog udjela penzije na bivšeg partnera. Alternativno, ljudi mogu kompenzirati penziju drugom imovinom – na primjer, jedan partner može dobiti veći udio u porodičnoj kući u zamjenu za to da drugi zadrži svoju penziju. Neki se dogovore da prime jednokratnu isplatu kada njihov partner ode u penziju. Gospodin Webb je priznao da nema 'brzih rješenja' za ovaj problem, ali je naglasio važnost veće svijesti o budućoj vrijednosti penzija kod ljudi koji se razvode. Rekao je: ‘U teoriji, imamo podjelu penzije prilikom razvoda. ‘Međutim, u stvarnosti to ne funkcionira baš dobro. Prosječan advokat za razvode fokusiran je na kuću, a ako još uvijek imate djecu, da li ćete se stvarno žestoko boriti za udio u penziji?’. Advokatica za porodično pravo Marilyn Stowe je izjavila da supružnik s nižim primanjima često dobije trenutnu imovinu, poput kuće ili novca, dok se dugoročna imovina poput penzija često 'ostavlja drugoj strani'. Rekla je: ‘Slažem se da dugoročne potrebe nikada ne bi trebalo zanemariti, ali okolnosti obično daju prednost trenutnim potrebama.’ Gospođa Stowe je rekla da advokatske firme i sudovi 'nikada ne bi zaboravili tako vrijednu imovinu' u pregovorima, ali parovi koji postignu neformalni sporazum mogu pogriješiti. Dodala je: ‘S obzirom na to da pravna pomoć više nije dostupna za razvod, mnogi parovi mogu pomisliti da ne mogu priuštiti advokata i mogli bi previdjeti vrijednost penzija.’ Caroline Abrahams, iz organizacije Age UK, je rekla: ‘Važno je da se svi ohrabruju da štede novac za starost. ‘Age UK vjeruje da bi starijim osobama trebalo ponuditi periodične 'finansijske provjere' kako bi znali koliko su finansijski sigurni. To uključuje razumijevanje, ako ste u braku, šta se događa s vašom penzijom kada vaš partner umre ili ako se vaša situacija promijeni iz drugih razloga.’

article_content: Getting children to open up about sexual abuse, particularly when it involves a family member, is notoriously difficult. Artist Saint Hoax has incorporated Disney princesses into his message to young victims, hoping this visual language will resonate. 'The aim of the poster series is to encourage victims to report their cases so the authorities can prevent future occurrences,' the Middle East-based artist told MailOnline. The impactful posters depict three iconic Disney characters—Aurora from 'Sleeping Beauty,' Ariel from 'The Little Mermaid,' and Princess Jasmine from 'Aladdin'—in uncomfortable lip-locks with their fathers. 'I recently learned that a close friend was molested by her father when she was seven,' Saint Hoax explains. 'It took her 14 years to share that traumatizing experience, which deeply affected me.' He adds: 'As an artist and activist, I decided to highlight this issue in a new way. I used Disney princesses because their image is familiar to my target audience.' Saint Hoax says he initially contacted a major organization, hoping they would use the campaign, but received no response. He then published the work independently, after which several foundations fighting child sexual abuse and incest shared the images. The project has elicited mixed reactions. One commenter on Jezebel wrote: '[Children] now associate a beloved cartoon and childhood escapism with incest.' Another wrote: 'Creepy and disturbing, but not actually helpful.' However, others view it differently, with one supporter saying: 'Using Disney princesses makes sense... Because of the characters' familiarity, these images are creepy and uncomfortable, which is exactly what they should be.' Interestingly, the original version of 'Sleeping Beauty,' written in the 16th century, depicts the princess being raped by a king during her slumber, unbeknownst to most Disney fans. Saint Hoax reveals that, just one day after publishing the posters, they had already made a difference to one girl. 'I received an email from a girl thanking me for the project, saying she decided to report her father after seeing the posters. I actually cried,' he says. 'I'm so glad I published the series. If the posters change one person's life, it's worth it.' One of the Disney characters used in the campaign turns out to be a particularly fitting choice. In the original 'Sleeping Beauty' story, the princess isn't awakened by a prince's kiss. While asleep, a king rapes her, and she later gives birth to twins. The princess awakens to find herself in a very different situation than in later versions of the story. Saint Hoax, based in the Middle East, uses a pseudonym to protect himself and his provocative campaigns due to strict censorship in the region. His previous work includes cartoon characters from 'Aladdin' appearing on 'denied' visa applications from the UK and representations of political figures like Barack Obama and Kim Jong Un. He received 'a lot of threats' after creating an image of King Abdullah of Saudi Arabia in drag. Saint Hoax describes his work as 'combining pop art with tyrants and world leaders.'

article_content: Mose Masoe believes Samoa is determined to 'shock the world' when they debut in the Four Nations against England in Brisbane. The St Helens prop forward missed Samoa's Pacific Cup victory over Fiji in May to focus on his first Super League season but has been recalled, along with Wakefield half-back/hooker Pita Godinet, for their upcoming matches. 'I was quite surprised to be selected,' Masoe said after his club's Grand Final win. 'They performed well against Fiji, but the coach kept faith in players who came over here. St Helens prop forward Mose Masoe is hoping to shock England with Samoa in the Four Nations. 'I'm really pleased to be selected again. This will be a great tournament. We have a strong squad, so we might surprise a few people. 'Our outside backs are skilled; some played in the Grand Final for the Bulldogs, and our forward pack can compete with the best. 'We showed our potential at the World Cup, and this is another step forward for us.' Masoe will be familiar with the opposition, and head coach Matt Parish can also rely on former St Helens and Great Britain scrum-half Sean Long, the Salford assistant who assisted during the World Cup and has flown to Brisbane for the Four Nations Series. Samoa will be without former St Helens forward Sia Soliola, who captained them in the World Cup, and preparations have been hampered by the suspension of three players following a nightclub incident. Parish had to exclude Canterbury Bulldogs forward Reni Maitua (a teammate of England's acting captain James Graham), North Queensland Cowboys centre Tautau Moga, and Wests Tigers back-rower Sauaso Sue, while Canterbury centre Tim Lafai is unavailable due to his wedding.
